existing.description: Fellowship at NIAS for researchers in the field of applied monetary economics, macro-economics or public finance
eligibility: Have a minimum of three years of post-PhD academic experience
Be based in the Netherlands or abroad
Work in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics, macroeconomic policy, public finance or public finance policy
Be a prominent, leading mid- to late-career researcher, or a promising early-career talent, in the Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation's priority fields
Have a good command of English, the working language at NIAS
Be willing and able to be present at NIAS four working days per week for the duration of the semester
existing.eligibility_summary: Researchers from the Netherlands or abroad with a minimum of three years of post-PhD academic experience, working in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics, macroeconomic policy, public finance or public finance policy. The fellowship is aimed primarily at prominent mid- to late-career researchers, while exceptionally talented early-career researchers are also eligible and encouraged to apply.
benefits: Personal stipend, or a Dutch University Grant paid to the home institution
Five or ten months of research time at NIAS
Office at NIAS and access to research facilities and library services
Subsidised accommodation where eligible, or reimbursement of local public transport
Participation in the academic, community and outreach programmes
Membership of a multidisciplinary international research community
Opportunity to meet Dutch academics, policymakers and representatives of financial institutions
coverage: Personal stipend, or a Dutch University Grant paid to the home institution for fellows affiliated with a Dutch university or research institute
Office at NIAS and access to research facilities and library services
Subsidised accommodation where eligible, or reimbursement of local public transport
requirements: Submit the application through the online application form
Keep the project proposal to no more than 1,500 words including footnotes, excluding references and abstract
Reflect in the proposal on how the research would benefit from and contribute to the multidisciplinary NIAS research community
Be present at NIAS four working days per week for the duration of the semester
documents: Full project proposal of no more than 1,500 words including footnotes, with references and abstract excluded
existing.english_requirement: The working language at NIAS is English. Applicants must have a good command of English in order to contribute effectively to the fellows' community and to receive input on their own research.
application_method: Apply during the published call window via the online application form
Upload the full project proposal within the word limit
Submit before the call closes on the published closing date
existing.selection_notes: The Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation gives particular priority to researchers with an outstanding record in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics or public finance. Applicants are encouraged to reflect on the collaborative and multidisciplinary environment at NIAS and to consider how their research might both benefit from and contribute to the NIAS research community and beyond.
existing.best_fit: An established researcher with at least three years of post-PhD experience and a strong publication record in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics or public finance, who can spend five or ten months in Amsterdam and wants to engage with Dutch policymakers and financial institutions.
existing.notes: The Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation was established in 2007 in honour of Willem F. Duisenberg to foster excellence in economic research in the Netherlands, and is supported by De Nederlandsche Bank, the Dutch Ministry of Finance and several major Dutch financial institutions: ING Group, Rabobank Nederland, ABN AMRO and AEGON. The Foundation has no employees and receives administrative and organisational support from NIAS. Its board consists of Chair Prof. Dr Klaas Knot, Treasurer Prof. dr. Antoine Buyse (Director NIAS) and Board Member Joanne Kellermann; board members receive no remuneration. The funding route depends on affiliation: a personal stipend for the fellow, or a Dutch University Grant paid to the institution for fellows at a Dutch university or research institute. NIAS publishes no euro amount for either route.
existing.duration: 5 to 10 months, as either a five-month or a ten-month semester
existing.application_period: Annual; the published 2027-2028 call ran from 15 January to 13 April 2026, one five-month and one ten-month fellowship awarded per academic year
existing.deadline_display: The call for the 2027-2028 academic year is open from 15 January to 13 April 2026.
existing.program_type: Residual research fellowship in economics at a national advanced-study institute, funded by the Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation
